verdict.rationale: Oneleet documents a built-in policy template library in two tiers (Formal minimum-viable and Comprehensive) that users customize. It also has a draft/publish workflow on the Policies page, and the reference to drafts that "don't require review" implies a review step for others. That covers roughly half the story. Missing for 10: evidence of lawyer-grade or legally vetted templates, a documented in-app policy editor, policy version history, an explicit approval workflow, per-employee policy acceptance tracking, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a founder, policies come from a lawyer-grade template library with an editor, versioning, approvals, and per-employee acceptance tracking

citations.quote: Our platform offers two types of policy templates to assist you in this process: Formal (Minimum Viable Policies)... Comprehensive
When customizing the templates, focus on adjusting the language to reflect your organization’s practices without altering the core intent of the policies.
On the **Policies** page, choose **Publish draft policies** to publish drafts that don’t require review.
